content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 14 and 30. Supplemental: SEI ATAM and Views and Beyond. This unit focuses on capstone architecture package.

The capstone brings the course together. Students define scope, identify stakeholders, write scenarios, choose views, document decisions, apply perspectives, evaluate tradeoffs, and present an architecture package.
A strong final package does not need to be huge. It needs to be coherent, source-backed, stakeholder-aware, explicit about tradeoffs, and honest about risks and assumptions.

Capstone: produce an architecture package for a medium-sized software system with context, functional, information, deployment, operational, two perspectives, five decision records, and an evaluation summary.

concepts.name: Capstone architecture package
concepts.description: A final course artifact combining architecture scope, views, decisions, perspectives, risks, and evaluation evidence.

concepts.name: Architecture coherence
concepts.description: The degree to which views, decisions, rationale, scenarios, and constraints tell a consistent architectural story.

concepts.name: Risk register
concepts.description: A maintained list of architectural risks, impacts, owners, mitigation actions, and status.

concepts.name: Architecture presentation
concepts.description: A structured communication of architecture decisions, tradeoffs, and evidence to stakeholders.
